native_text_pages:
CHITKARAU – AN EDUCATIONAL EXPERIENCE OF MIND & SPIRIT.
COME, EXPLORE YOUR POTENTIAL 
 
We are nestled at the foothills of the mighty Himalayas in the most planned, secure, and
beautiful city of Chandigarh, designed by French Architect Le Corbusier, with two spectacular
campuses. The city boasts of a dense green cover, easy accessibility by air, road, and rail, and
sumptuous Indian and Western cuisines from all parts of India and the world. Yoga, mindfulness,
and meditation are practiced at the campus with unforgettable trips in the Himalayas, and so
much more. This brochure is a window to all the opportunities India and Chitkara University will
throw up for you. Come explore us, and your Potential

The Golden Temple in Amritsar, officially Harmandir Sahib, is Sikhism’s holiest shrine and a
masterpiece of sacred architecture. Nestled within a shimmering man-made pool called the Amrit
Sarovar, its gilded façade and marble inlays reflect the devotion of generations. Pilgrims and visitors of
all faiths come to offer prayers, listen to continuous recitation of the Guru Granth Sahib, and partake
in the langar, a free community meal served to thousands daily. The temple’s peaceful atmosphere,
historic significance, and commitment to equality and service make it a symbol of spiritual solace and
communal harmony in India, welcoming seekers from everywhere.

TANTALIZE YOUR TASTE
BUDS 
INDIAN CUISINE 
Cook, taste, and learn
diverse Indian cuisines in
our culinary sessions!

REJUVENATE
YOUR
BODY MIND
and soul
Join our refreshing campus
yoga sessions for balance and
energy!

WE ARE AT THE FOREFRONT OF INTERNATIONAL ENGAGEMENT & PARTNERSHIPS
 
Name any part of the World, and we send and receive students. From North America to Europe,
the Middle East to Southeast Asia, from Japan & Korea to down under Australia, our students go
everywhere, and we welcome their students to Chitkara University. Chandigarh is the most well-
planned, secure, and non-polluted Indian city in the foothills of the Himalayas, where our
international students and faculty love to keep coming back. 
Chitkara University offers a diverse range of programs in Engineering, Business, Pharmacy, Health
Sciences, Design, Media, Hospitality, Education, Law, and more. With a student-centric approach,
the university ensures holistic development by combining academic rigor with practical exposure,
entrepreneurship, and skill enhancement. 
 
Our experiential learning is not just limited to academic education but a holistic one that engages
and rejuvenates your mind and body alike. From Yoga to Meditation, trekking and soul searching
trips in the upper reaches of the Himalayas, students experience a vibe and energy of India that it
has represented for centuries. Besides, you will be welcomed to learn and indulge in vibrant and
lip-smacking Indian cuisines from diverse parts of India, and create some lifelong relationships with
our community that could be a bedrock support for life. 
 
You can come to us for a short mobility or a semester or global internships, we abide by our motto
‘Athithi Devo Bhava’, which simply translates to our guests are our Gods. Come, experience our
Hospitality and grow in your mind and spirit at Chitkara University

His Holiness 14th Dalai Lama at the
Global Week 2019

Student Exchange Program
FACT SHEET
2027 Spring

■ General Information of the Institution
■ Office of International Affairs

Website  www.seoultech.ac.kr

■ Application Documents (in English)

No. Document Notes
1 TB test result  - Negative Tuberculosis(TB) test result
 - Available tests: Chest X-ray, blood test OR skin test
2 M easles Vaccination Certificate  - Proof of 2 doses

■ Language requirement
 Applicants are required to have a good command of either English (B2 level) OR Korean (TOPIK Level 3) 
in order to communicate and function effectively in an academic environment. Therefore, an 
internationally recognized language certificate equivalent to these levels is required.
 ▶ TOEIC 750 / IELTS 5.5 / TOEFL 72 / Cambridge English Scale 160 / Global Scale of English 
(Pearson) 59 / DET 100
    OR
 ▶ TOPIK(Test of Proficiency in Korean) Level 3
    ※ Students who apply to the exchange program using a TOPIK score will be permitted to 
enroll in Korean-language-taught courses only.
■ Number of exchanges students
 Due to accommodation capacity and course registration constraints, SeoulTech has implemented 
a strategic enrollment limitation starting from the 2024 academic year. This decision reflects our 
commitment to maintaining high standards of education, fostering a conducive learning 
environment, and ensuring that each student receives personalized attention and support.
 We will strive to maintain a balanced number of inbound and outbound exchange students.
 If none of SeoulTech students have participated in your exchange program during the past two 
semesters only one open seat will be allocated to your university. 
 Please note that we are unable to accept more than two students from each partner university 
per semester. If there is any uncertainty regarding the quota, we strongly recommend contacting 
SeoulTech in advance before beginning your selection process.
■ Academic Calendar
■ Courses
 - Course List (https://global.seoultech.ac.kr/bound/inbound/course)
   The finalized list of courses offered in English for each semester will be announced 
approximately one month before the start of the semester. In the meantime, please refer to 
the course list from the previous semester. Please note that exchange students are allowed to 
select courses only from the Module list.
 - Syllabus
   For students’ convenience, we have gathered all the syllabi for the Module courses on Google Drive.
   ▶ (2026 Spring Semester)
       https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1IGgr8Y7103xdRg0X1qAMuHqznIbMtXmJ?usp=sharing
   ▶ (2026 Fall Semester)
       https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1wzP4AnJfZKSYiJqh7XX_MxEePq3Pf0rf?usp=sharing
  ※ Please note that course offerings are relatively flexible and may be added or removed for the upcom ing 
semester. Therefore, students whose home universities have strict academic requirements, such as specific 
mandatory courses, should be aware that our university cannot guarantee the availability of particular courses.
3. Academic Information
 2027 Spring Semester  March 2, 2027 ~ June 21, 2027

■ Intensive Korean Language Course Program  (https://klc.seoultech.ac.kr/en/course/registration/)
 Exchange students may enroll in an intensive Korean Language Course Program. This is a 
non-credit course, and students are required to pay the tuition fee.
■ Grading System
 All exchange students can take (Min) 2 credits ~ (Max) 18 credits per semester.
 1 Credit = 16 teaching hours including lectures, exam, assignments, and attendance
 1 Course = 2 or 3 credits
 All courses are offered on a semester basis and run for 16 weeks.
■ Assessment
※ The lowest passing grade is D0(60.)
※ Assessment can be subject to change

■ On campus
 SeoulTech does not guarantee accommodation for exchange students.
 ※ Dormitory fees can be subject to change
 ※ For Sunglim International Hall Dormitory, spaces are extremely limited and current residents 
are given priority to extend their stay for the following semester. Consequently, the likelihood 
of being assigned to this hall is very low. Therefore, applications for the Sunglim International 
Hall Dormitory are accepted on a waiting list basis only. 
 * Dormitory Meal Fee (Can only use from Dormitory Cafeteria)

4. Accommodation

■ Off campus
 SeoulTech does not collaborate with any private housing companies. Housing information is 
provided solely for students’ convenience. 
 ※ If any dispute arises between a housing provider and a student, the university will not assume 
any responsibility.
 * Blessing in Seoul : https://blessing-in.seoulhotelspage.com/en/
 * Stay14 : www.stay14.com
 * Goshipages : https://goshipages.com/ko
 * Borderless House: https://www.borderless-house.com/kr/
 * Ziptoss: https://global.ziptoss.com/en/
 * enkostay: https://stay.enko.kr/ 
 * HaniSeoul: https://www.haniseoul.com/
 * Airbnb
■ Visa
 - Exchange students are required to obtain a student visa (D-2-6) to study in Korea. Students 
must apply for their D-2-6 visa prior to arrival.
    ※ A visitor visa cannot be converted into a student visa from within Korea. Pursuing studies 
under a K-ETA (Tourist Visa) is strictly prohibited.
 
 - Following the Ministry of Justice’s updated regulations and tightened immigration policies 
introduced in June 2022, additional documentation is now required for exchange students.
    ※ The document list below is for reference only. Please be sure to contact the embassy or 
consulate of your home country to verify the exact required documents for your visa.
 ▶ Nationals of OECD countries
   - Certificate of Admission
   - Letter of Acceptance
   - Certificate of Business Registration
 ▶ Nationals of Non-OECD countries
   - Certificate of Admission
   - Letter of Acceptance
   - Certificate of Business Registration
   - Certificate of Enrollment
    ⋅ For Apostille member countries: Must be notarized with an Apostille 
    ⋅ For non-Apostille countries: Must be authenticated by the Korean Embassy
   - Bank statement: The statement must demonstrate sufficient funds to cover living expenses 
during the exchange period (USD 6,000 for one semester / USD 12,000 for 
one academic year).
   
5. Visa

■ National Health Insurance Service (NHIS)
 National Health Insurance is a mandatory program implemented by the Ministry of Health and 
Welfare in Korea and is not optional. It applies regardless of whether students have private 
insurance. Once students apply for their Alien Registration Card (ARC) after arrival in Korea and 
the physical card is issued, their information will be updated in the National Health Insurance 
system, and they will be automatically enrolled.
 As of 2026, the monthly National Health Insurance premium is KRW 79,310. Payment notices are 
sent each month to the student’s registered residence in Korea.
■ Korean buddy program & International Student Club (ISC)
 ISC (International Student Club) is a student organization at SeoulTech that operates a buddy 
program for international students. During their stay in Korea, exchange students are supported 
by ISC members to help make their campus life more enjoyable and enriching.

How to get to Zlín
Zlín, a vibrant Moravian city in the Czech Republic, is well-connected by various transportation options. Whether you want to get here by plane, train, bus, or car, here is how you can reach Zlín efficiently:
By plane
Unfortunately, Zlín does not have its international airport. The Václav Havel Airport Prague (PRG) is the air gate to the Czech Republic with daily connections from/to major European cities. More information about flight timetables and transport connections from/to the airport are available on the website of
Václav Havel Airport Prague
. There are reliable and frequent connections from Prague airport to the city center by
public transport
and
special airport buses
(AE – Airport Express). There is the possibility of buying tickets, including from/to airport transport and tickets for connecting buses/trains to Zlín.
Other options frequently used by our international students are to fly to Bratislava (Slovakia) – approx. 150km from Zlín, Vienna (Austria) – approx. 180km from Zlín, Katowice (Poland) – approx. 215km from Zlín, or Kraków (Poland) – approx. 290km from Zlín. There are train or bus connections to Zlín from all of these cities.
By train
The Czech Republic has an extensive railway network, operated by four major railway companies:
České dráhy
(ČD, Czech Railways),
RegioJet
,
LEO Express
,
and
Arriva
. The timetables and connections are changing approximately once per year. Due to that, we recommend checking the connections at the websites of the mentioned railway companies.
Zlín itself has several train stations even though they are all quite small. The main train station is called
Zlín – Střed
and it has only one direct train from Prague (
Zlínský expres
). However, the neighbouring town
Otrokovice
is placed on the main train corridor. Due to that, it is possible to get directly from Otrokovice to five European capitals (Bratislava, Budapest, Prague, Vienna, and Warsaw). So, it is possible to search for the connections to Otrokovice and then use the public transportation working between Zlín and Otrokovice.
Traveling by České dráhy
Tickets are sold at most of the train stations, and it is not mandatory to purchase your tickets online. However, we recommend buying them online because the online reservation goes together with the free seat reservation inside the train. Then you can download the ticket to your mobile device without the necessity of printing it for the domestic trains. The international trains might require a ticket to be printed due to the incompatibility of national systems. The company provides first- and second-class travel. Most of the scheduled trains stop at Otrokovice, where it is possible to change for a local train going in the direction of Zlín Střed, or it is possible to use the public transportation mentioned above.
Traveling by RegioJet
RegioJet provides service on the arterial train lines. In combination with their buses, it is possible to get to Zlín from major Czech cities. If you travel with RegioJet, we highly recommend you buy your tickets online. From Prague, it is possible to take their yellow train from the main Prague train station to Olomouc, where a connecting RegioJet bus to Zlín is available.
Traveling by LEO Express
LEO Express trains go from Prague main train station to Přerov, where you can change to a bus or a train to Zlín. The company no longer operates trains, or buses to Zlín, or Otrokovice.
Traveling by Arriva
At this moment, there are no train connections provided by Arriva on the track between Prague and Zlín. Nevertheless, Arriva operates several regional train tracks in the Zlín region.
By bus
If you do not like traveling by train, you can use a large network of coach lines instead. Usually, buses are more frequent, and slightly cheaper than trains. The Czech Republic has connections from/to major European cities several times a week. Most international buses arrive in Prague (Florenc AN) or Brno (Zvonařka AN). Several buses get you to Zlín from Prague and Brno each day. Further information on train and bus connections within the Czech Republic is available at
idos.cz
.
By car
Zlín is connected to the Czech motorway network thanks to highways D49 and D55. You can easily get to the country’s major cities (Brno, Olomouc, Ostrava, and Prague) from here. In the Czech Republic, it is mandatory to have an e-vignette for using a
motorway
. There are four available versions of the e-vignettes:
1 day for
CZK 210
(EUR 8.40; USD 8.95)
10 days for
CZK 290
(EUR 11.60; USD 12.35)
1 month for
CZK 460
(EUR 18.35; USD 19.60)
1 year for
CZK 2,440
(EUR 97.40; USD 103.90)
All the sales points for the e-vignettes can be found online
here
or you can purchase them directly via the
official e-shop
.
Connection search
Information on all domestic and most international connections of trains and buses is possible to find at
idos.cz
. We also recommend the mobile app for
Android
or
iOS
with the same name. It is always possible to find the desired connections there.
Public transportation in Zlín
Once you are in Zlín, the city has a well-organized public transport system, including trolleybuses and buses. Tickets are available at kiosks, ticket machines, directly in the trolley/buses, via mobile apps, or from the driver. The following single tickets are available:
One-ride
ticket for
30 minutes for CZK 18
(EUR 0.72; USD 0.77)
One-ride
ticket for
60 minutes for CZK 24
(EUR 0.95; USD 1.00)
One-ride
ticket purchased from driver for
60 minutes for CZK 30
(EUR 1.20; USD 1.30)
One-use
ticket for luggage, or an animal for
60 minutes for CZK 18
(EUR 0.72; USD 0.77)
There are also daily or weekly tickets available:
One-day
ticket (24 hours) for
CZK 100
(EUR 4.00; USD 4.25)
One-week
ticket (168 hours) for
CZK 270
(EUR 10.80; USD 11.50)
Zlín’s public transport system is divided into five (5) different zones, while the tickets you can get are valid in all zones:
Zone A
is Zlín’s wider centre.
Zone B
is valid for the outskirts of Zlín.
Zone C
is valid for neighboring town Otrokovice and a few smaller villages.
Zone D
is only for train connections to Želechovice nad Dřevnicí
Zone E
is only for train connections to Lípa nad Dřevnicí, Zádveřice, and Vizovice.
Bolt
Since autumn 2024, Bolt is available in Zlín and in the wider area around the regional capital. All requests for rides are booked through the mobile app (
Android
, or
iOS
) that connects a customer with the driver for a guaranteed and previously agreed price.

Basic information
Welcome to the Faculty of Education UWB
As an Erasmus student coming to study in Pilsen at the Faculty of Education, you can choose any course from the sections mentioned below. Check with your university how many credits you need to bring back and choose courses according to your preferences. Keep in mind that your courses should be linked to what you study at your home university. It is up to your university which courses they recognize.
Feel free to combine courses from all the sections (see below).
If you have any questions, contact us. We are here for you.
Contacts

FAQ
Here you will find answers to the most common questions about studying and living in Plzeň. Our FAQ is designed to help you prepare for your stay and make your arrival smoother.
Are there any required travel documents?
Do I need international insurance?
How do I get a passport or visa? Do I need a visa?
How can I budget for my study abroad?
Where can I buy inexpensive flights?

Are there any required travel documents?
Yes, you will need a valid passport to enter the Czech Republic. Depending on your nationality, you may also need a visa or residence permit. Make sure your passport is valid for the entire duration of your stay.
Back
Do I need international insurance?
Yes. All incoming students are required to have valid health insurance that covers medical care in the Czech Republic. EU/EEA students can use their European Health Insurance Card (EHIC). Non-EU students must arrange private health insurance approved for use in the Czech Republic.
Back
How do I get a passport or visa? Do I need a visa?
If you are from the EU/EEA or Switzerland, you do not need a visa to study in the Czech Republic. Students from other countries will need to apply for a long-term visa or residence permit. Please contact the Czech Embassy or Consulate in your home country for details.
Back
How can I budget for my study abroad?
The cost of living in the Czech Republic is relatively affordable compared to many European countries. On average, students should budget around 400–700 EUR per month for accommodation, food, transportation, and personal expenses. Keep in mind that travel, study materials, and leisure activities may add extra costs.
Back
Where can I buy inexpensive flights?
Popular platforms such as Skyscanner, Kiwi, or Google Flights can help you compare prices. For flights within Europe, low-cost airlines (e.g., Ryanair, Wizz Air, EasyJet) often offer budget-friendly options. Booking in advance usually ensures better prices.
Back
Where can I find lodging abroad?
Our university provides student dormitories, which are the most affordable and convenient option. If you prefer private housing, you can explore rental websites, student Facebook groups, or real estate agencies in Plzeň. We recommend arranging accommodation before your arrival.
Back
What should I pack?
Pack according to the length of your stay and the seasons. Winters in the Czech Republic can be cold (down to -10 °C), so bring warm clothing, while summers can be hot. Don’t forget essentials such as travel documents, insurance papers, medications, study materials, and adaptors for European sockets (Type C/E).
Back
How do I stay safe while traveling abroad?
The Czech Republic is considered a safe country. Still, follow general safety rules: keep your documents in a secure place, be cautious in crowded areas, and know the local emergency number (112). It is also a good idea to register with your embassy and stay informed about local laws and customs.
Back
How do I get from the airport to Plzeň?
Most international students arrive via Prague Airport (Václav Havel Airport). From there, you can take a direct bus or use public transport to reach the main train or bus station in Prague. Regular trains and buses connect Prague to Plzeň, and the journey takes about 1–1.5 hours. Tickets cost around 5–10 EUR.
Back
What student support services are available?
The International Office and the Study Department are here to help you with academic and administrative issues. The university also offers counseling services, a Career Centre, a library, and IT support. Through the Buddy Program, local students can help you settle in and navigate your new environment.
Back
What are the language requirements? Do I need to speak Czech?
Courses for international students are offered in English, so Czech is not required for studying. However, learning some basic Czech phrases can be very useful for everyday life, such as shopping or traveling. Some faculties even offer free or low-cost Czech language courses for international students.
Back
Can I work while studying in the Czech Republic?
EU/EEA and Swiss students can work without restrictions. Non-EU students are allowed to work part-time during their studies, but depending on the type of visa, some restrictions may apply. It is recommended to check the exact conditions with the Czech Ministry of Interior.
Back
What public transportation is available in Plzeň?
Plzeň has an excellent public transport system including trams, buses, and trolleybuses. Students can buy discounted monthly passes (around 12–15 EUR) for unlimited travel. Tickets are available at kiosks, online, or via mobile apps.
Back
What is your question?
Plzeň is a vibrant university city with a rich cultural scene. Students can join various clubs, sports activities, and student organizations. There are concerts, festivals, and plenty of opportunities to explore Czech traditions as well as international communities. You can take a look on
https://www.visitplzen.eu/en/
Back
Where can I find information about courses and registration?
All course information is available in the university’s online system (STAG). The Study Department and your faculty coordinators will guide you through course registration and requirements before the semester begins.
Back
What is the cost of student dormitories and meals?
Dormitory accommodation usually costs 100–130 EUR per month, depending on the type of room. Student canteens (menza) offer affordable meals starting from 2–4 EUR. Many students combine dormitory living with cooking or eating out in local restaurants, which are also reasonably priced
Back
Whom can I contact in case of emergency?
In the Czech Republic, the general emergency number is
112
. You can also directly call the police (158), ambulance (155), or fire service (150). At the university, the International Office and your student buddy can help you in urgent situations.
Back

Academic Credit System
SeoulTech offers the following Inbound Programs:
▶ Student Exchange Program
:
Students can enroll in up to six academic credit courses.
* The Student Exchange Program at SeoulTech allows students from
partner universities
to pursue their studies for one or two semesters at SeoulTech.
* Students who are officially nominated by their home universities will have the opportunity to apply for the Student Exchange Program at SeoulTech.
* Tuition will be waived under the student exchange agreement.
▶
Visiting(Fee-paying) Program
:
Students can enroll in up to six academic credit courses.
* Open to students enrolled at
both partner and non-partner universities
of SeoulTech.
* Participants will have the chance to take credit courses to pursue their studies for one or two semesters at SeoulTech.
* Students must be officially nominated by their home universities.
* Although students in the Visiting Program are granted the same status as exchange students, they are not eligible for tuition waivers.
■
Eligibility
Exchange student who wishes to study at SeoulTech must;
- Completed at least (Undergraduate) two semesters / (Graduate) one semester at student’s home university
- Be enrolled as a full-time student at home university that has an active student exchange agreement with SeoulTech
- Be nominated as an exchange student candidate by student home university
- Be able to study in either English or Korean for at least one semester (4.5 months)
- Have not studied at any other Korean university in the previous semester

Application Documents

(※ original required to SeoulTech)

正文
Reader's Guide
Welcome to Xiamen University Libraries. This Guide will help you navigate the library to find books and articles, study spaces, facilities, and different ways of getting in touch with librarians. We hope that you will find the guide useful in your library research and that you have an enjoyable experience using the Libraries.
Libraries
The Library consists of seven libraries, including Main Library, Dewang Library, Tan KahKee College Library, Economics & Business Library, Information & Engineering Library, Law Library, and Art Library.
Library Cards
Xiamen University registered students, faculty, instructors, lecturers and staffs use campus card as library card for borrowing materials and for access to libraries and other areas requiring a library card. All library privileges are required to have library card activated first.
For inter-university exchange program students, library card will be activated automatically within one week after registration in XMU International Students'''' Affairs Division.
For college-invited exchange students, a borrowing application form completely filled out, signed and sealed by the college, personnel ID/Passport along with campus card are required to activate campus card’s library privileges. The Service Counter of Main Library or Dewang Library is where users can activate campus card, and ask questions about borrowing privileges and responsibilities. Library privileges are not transferable. Only the individual named on the library card can use the card. For a downloadable borrowing application form, please visit
http://library.xmu.edu.cn/portal-en/secondpage.asp?pid=5&sid=4772
.

All material is subject to recall by another user. Once recalled, item due dates will be shortened to 22 days from the borrowing date, and item that has been kept more than 15 days should be returned within one week.
Return
Return materials to any library circulation desk during open hours, or to the outdoor book drops when libraries are closed. Materials damaged or incomplete should be brought immediately to the owning library circulation desk to discuss repair or replacement options that may be available.
Fines and Fees
For each overdue material, users will be charged RMB 0.2 per day. Borrowing privileges will be blocked until overdue items are returned and fines are paid. Paid overdue fines or replacement fees couldn’t be refunded. Overdue notices are a courtesy, sent to the email address provided in users’ library. Failure to receive a notice does not cancel obligations to pay fines or fees.
Study Space
Xiamen University Libraries offer the opportunity to make use of study seats at the majority of service locations. There are differences across the individual locations as to whether study seats should be reserved and booked in advance, or whether they are free to use on an ad hoc basis. Detailed seat management rules and step-by-step instructions could be found at
http://library.xmu.edu.cn/portal-en/seatmanage.asp
. Xiamen University Libraries also offer online booking service for group study rooms on the 2nd to 4th floor of Main Library through
http://rooms.xmulib.org/en
, and group study rooms on the 5th floor of Dewang Library through
http://172.19.254.242/studyroom/EN/Default.aspx
.
Print, Copy and Scan
Xiamen University Libraries offer a campus-wide, cloud-based printing service, which allows users to send print requests to print-copy-scan machines located in the libraries. In order to print from personal device, download and install the correct print drivers. Machine locations and detailed instructions could be found at
http://210.34.4.89/
. English version could be found by switching language icon on the up right side. Detailed instructions are also available in self-service printing, copying, and scanning area.
Wireless Internet Access (Wi-Fi)
All library locations offer free wireless access (Wi-Fi) in public areas at all times the libraries are open. Options for Wi-Fi access in the library include XMUNET+ and Eduroam. Use personal device''''s network utilities, and look for the network you would like to use. “XMUNET+” requires users to log in Student/Faculty Identification Number and password, which could be setup on the website of
http://p.xmu.edu.cn
. The advantage of using Eduroam over the other networks is that it can be used at other universities that are part of the Eduroam network.
Off Campus Access
Xiamen University students, faculty and staff may access Xiamen University Only materials via connecting from off campus through VPN (Virtual Private Network) Services. Step-by-step instructions and examples could be found at
http://library.xmu.edu.cn/portal-en/proxy.asp
. Before accessing licensed article databases, eBooks and eJournals off campus, make sure to read Conditions of Use and Licensing Restrictions for Electronic Resources. It is the responsibility of individual users to ensure their use of electronic resources does not breach the terms and conditions specified in the license agreements. Lists of digital library resources could be found on the website of
http://library.xmu.edu.cn/portal-en/database.asp?language=eng
.
Interlibrary Loan Services and Fees
Xiamen University Libraries is networked with libraries around the world to obtain materials that are not available. Interlibrary Borrowing assists Xiamen University students, faculty, and staff to obtain books, articles, and other materials not available in teaching, learning and research. Most libraries charge us for loaning materials and for delivering electronic files. We charge RMB 0.2 per page for photocopy or delivery in electronic formats of articles, proceeding papers, ordinary books and dissertations. For rare books scanning, each page fees range from RMB 2-15. For each printed book delivery, we charge users RMB 15.
Campus Card Services
The campus card integrates various functions, such as personal identification, system login and campus payment. In the event of a lost or card-locked, please visit one of the following service counters to report loss, reissue or unlock the campus card (Tel: 2183508).

XMU e-card
XMU e-card is issued by Xiamen University, combining the functions of the student ID, library, dining, shopping in campus, etc.
A. Functions
With the XMU e-card, you can live and study in XMU easily without taking too much cash or bank cards. XMU e-card involves information about your student number, name, e-card account, your photo and other personal information, which is useful when dining in the campus cafeteria, entering libraries, borrowing books and shopping in campus.
B. Payment and Recharge
Please link your bank account with your e-card in the bank, then you can easily top up your e-card by transferring money from the bank card to e-card on self-service machines near the cafeteria, maximum 500RMB per time. Cash is not accepted for recharging e-cards. The default password is 123456 and you'd better change it on self-service machines and e-card website as soon as you have the card.
C. Relevant Addresses:
XMU E-card center is located on the 1st floor, Jiageng Building No.3. 24-hour voice call: 2187890
l
Internet
Access
The University WLAN and WIFI is available in overseas students’ dormitory. Please go to China Telecom or China Unicom to purchase the WLAN or WIFI service pack.
For the campus WIFI service, please refer to this website
http://inc.xmu.edu.cn/14/92/c17101a332946/page.htm
for wireless network setup guide.
For Students who need the Internet service can go to the Xiamen University Information & network services Center with your student card.
Address: XMU Internet Center, 1st floor, Jiageng Building No. 3; Tel: 2183508.
Please refer to Xiamen University Information & network services for more information.
http://net.xmu.edu.cn/

l
Library
Located to the left of the South Gate, covering an area of 22,000 square meters, the XMU library holds over 2,500,000 volumes of books with 500,000 in foreign languages and the number of volumes grows by 100,000 every year. There are systematic book collections in subjects like economics, management, philosophy, history, mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology. Besides, XMU library is also for its characteristic materials in Southeast Asian Research and Taiwan Research. More than 40 famous international academic databases are rented or purchased by XMU. Web of Science and other world major academic databases are introduced. Now those databases available in the university LAN contain over 10,000 electronic journals in foreign languages and over 8,000 in language. Meanwhile, the total data amount saved in XMU local servers adds up to 8TB. You can visit the digital library on the Internet or enter the library or borrow the books with your XMU e-card.
l
Dining halls
Besides the dining hall and the coffee house on the first and second floor of Cai Qingjie Building, there are many other dining halls or cafeterias providing good meals and services for students. The following are their names and locations:

All the dining halls and canteens are provided with ultra-red sterilizing cupboard, ensuring high standard food hygiene. Students can buy food with XMU e-cards.

Xiada Post Office is at Yanwu Road near the campus. At the West Gate (main gate) of Xiamen University, there is an office for incoming and outgoing mail (Xiada Post Box). Letters sent to the students can be claimed at the reception on the second floor of Caiqingjie Building.
Any parcels sent from abroad can be collected by following procedures:
A. Pick up the Parcel-arrival notice at the dormitory reception;
B. Get the parcel form from Xiada Post Box by showing the Parcel-arrival notice and his/her own ID card;
C. Collect the parcel from Xiada Post Office.

Banks
Here are Bank of China, China Industrial and Commercial Bank, and China Construction Bank on XMU campus which offer services like currency saving deposit, time deposit, bank transfer, foreign currency transaction, etc.
l
Gymnasium and Stadium
There is a 400-meter standard track and field ground to the opposite side of Qunxian Building near the West Gate of the university. In front of the track and field ground, there are ten basketball courts and several horizontal and parallel bars. To the south of the track and field ground, there are tennis courts and volleyball courts. In front of Jiannan Great Hall, students will find the Shangxian (First Quarter of the Moon) Football Field containing two small football pitches where football lovers can demonstrate their ball skills. Besides that, eight new basketball courts have been set up between the Lingyun dormitory complex and Furong 12 dormitory building. Table-tennis rooms are located at Jianwen Building and Cai Qingjie Buildings. There is a swimming pool with standard tracks as well other facilities in the Qing Ming Swimming Gymnasium. In order to swim there, students need a health certificate issued by XMU Hospital and pay by XMU e-card.

If you are interested in living in student dorms located in the campus, please contact the school coordinator first to register the room or bring your admission acceptance letter to the reception of Cai Qingjie Building. Most of time, the dorms in the campus will be in high demand and reserved for full scholarship students.
Nanguang 4, Nanguang 5 Building and Cai Qingjie Building, located in the center of the main campus are dormitories specially for scholarship students, exchange students, and degreed students. With modern facilities such as air condition, television, telephone, internet access (optional), etc., the buildings provide comfortable accommodation, dining hall, coffee bar, store for overseas students
For more details, please contact: Cai Qingjie Building: Tel: 0086-592-2180501
Nanguang 5 Building: Tel: 0086-592-2182340
Cost:  RMB 30 per person per day, electricity & water not included for a twin bedroom, RMB 8 per person per day for a four-bedroom.

Welcome International Students 2026
Dear New Students：
Welcome to Tianjin University! In order to better embark on your new life ahead, please read the following notices regarding new-student registration.
Airport Pickup
Tianjin University has prepared free airport pick-up service for all new international students at the
Tianjin Binhai International Airport. For
individual who arrives at other airports, please arrange own transportation to the university for check-in and registration.
Arrangements for Airport Pick-up
Date:
31st Aug. to 2nd Sep.
Time:
9:00-21:00
Location:
Tianjin Binhai International Airport
After collecting check-in baggage, look for a volunteer carrying a sign board with "Tianjin University" written on it at the arrival hall, show your admission letter to the volunteer, after confirmation, you will be taken to the bus.
On-site Check-in
Date and Time
Foundation Program：
31st Aug. to 1st Sep.
Degree Program，General Scholar：
1st Sep. to 3rd Sep.
Location
The welcome stations of the university will be open from 29th Aug. to 4th Sep. Please confirm with your teacher from International Students' Affairs Office about the campus you will be study at and check-in at the specified welcome station for each campus:
Weijin Road Campus Welcome Station
Address：Block A&B, Liuyuan, Tianjin University, Weijin Road No.92, nankai District, Tianjin City
Peiyangyuan Campus Welcome Station
Address: Kela Apratment Block No.2, Tianjin University, Yaguan Road No.135, Jinnan District, Tianjin City
Procedures of Check-in
Step 1: Collect your Welcome Pack, which includes the New Student Guide, International Student Handbook, Campus ID Card, orientation schedule, campus map folder, registration procedure form and registration reminders.
Step 2: Verify your insurance payment receipt.
Step 3: Apply for a mobile SIM card.
Step 4: Open a bank account.
Step 5: Apply for on-campus accommodation or inquire about off-campus housing resources.
Step 6: Complete the 24-hour accommodation registration (record card for inspection).
Step 7: Make an appointment for physical examination for the day after check-in (payment is needed, You may go to the physical examination center via the bus the following day).
Registration
Time for Registration
The arrangement for registration for new international students of Weijin Road Campus:
Date: 2nd Sep. to 3rd Sep.
Time: 8:30 - 12:00, 13:00 - 16:30
Venue: Hall,Liuyuan, Weijin Road Campus, Tianjin University
The arrangement for registration for new international students of
Peiyangyuan Campus
:
Date: 4th Sep.
Time: 8:30 - 12:00, 13:00 - 16:30
Venue: Second Floor ofBlock A, Liuyuan, Peiyang Park Campus, Tianjin University
Documents Needed
Please get the documents prepared before check-in:
Registration Card (Obtain from the welcome station);
Original and photocopy of valid Passport and Visa (X1 or X2);
Electronic Admission Letter;
Electronic “Visa Application Form for Study in China” (Form JW201 or Form JW202);
Original and photocopy of highest degree certificate (Note: For new doctoral students, both bachelor’s and master’s degree certificates must be verified. Graduates from Chinese universities shall present your graduation certificate and degree certificate for verification. For new undergraduate students, the original high school graduation certificate shall be verified. Certificates issued in languages other than Chinese or English must be accompanied by notarized Chinese and English translation.);
10 passport size photos;
Original copy of “Foreigners Physical Examination Report” and blood test report (for students who plan to study in China for a period of more than 6 months);
Except for new students awarded CSC, CIS and MOF scholarships,  new students with other types of scholarships or self-funded new students shall complete online payment of registration fee, tuition fees, medical insurance fee and other required fees before arriving in China, and keep the payment receipts ready for registration.
Procedures of Registration
Step 1:
Pre-document Verification
Step 2:
Fee Payment
Step 3:
System Photo Capture
Step 4:
Personal Information Verification
Step 5:
Accommodation Information Registration
Step 6:
Academic Affairs Processing
Step 7:
China Entry-related Affairs Processing
Step 8:
Student Affairs Information Handover
Notes for Registration
Except for new students receiving CSC, CIS or MOF scholarships, those with other types of scholarships or self-funded students must submit the tuition payment certificate at registration. Failure to settle tuition will prevent completion of the registration process.
If you are unable to attend the centralized check-in and registration on
2nd Sep. to 4th Sep.
for personal reasons, you must complete the procedures in person at Office 401, International Education School Building, Weijin Road Campus, Tianjin University.
Students who cannot register on time must send an explanatory email to the Student Affairs Office of the International Education School of Tianjin University with a copy to the Admissions Office two weeks in advance. Failure to register on time without valid justification for more than two weeks will be regarded as a waiver of admission.
